findings.evidence:

AuthService.ts lines 38-42: signOut() calls supabase.auth.signOut() and logs warnings but never triggers account deletion. No file in the codebase contains any account deletion code (searched for 'deleteAccount', 'delete_account', 'apagar.conta', 'removeAccount', 'deletar', 'remove account'). **Critic Verification**: AuthContext.tsx lines 99-104: signOut() only calls supabase.auth.signOut() and clears local state — no remote account deletion. AuthService.ts lines 38-42: signOut() only calls supabase.auth.signOut(). No deleteAccount, delete_account, removeAccount, or similar function exists anywhere in the codebase. findings.issue_summary: App handles user accounts via Supabase Auth but NO in-app account deletion mechanism exists. The signOut() method only clears the local session without deleting the remote user record.
findings.recommendation: Implement in-app deletion: Create a highly discoverable path (e.g., under User Profile / Account Settings) to let users initiate account deletion directly in the app. The deletion must call a Supabase Admin API or Edge Function to permanently remove the user's remote database records, not merely sign them out.

findings.evidence:
Manifest: requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 (maxSdkVersion=28), READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 (maxSdkVersion=32). main.tsx:31 creates 'Biz-flow/' folder via Capacitor Filesystem mkdir(Directory.Documents). nativeFileService.ts writes/reads PDFs via Capacitor Filesystem to Directory.Documents/Biz-flow/. DocumentShareModal.tsx and useDocumentActions.ts similarly use Capacitor Filesystem scoped API. No direct Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() usage anywhere in the codebase. localStorage reference in assets is browser-level web storage, unrelated to Android file permissions.

**Critic Verification**: AndroidManifest.xml lines 55-58 declare WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=28) and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) with requestLegacyExternalStorage=true (line 11). All file operations in nativeFileService.ts, main.tsx, DocumentShareModal.tsx, and useDocumentActions.ts exclusively use the Capacitor Filesystem plugin with Directory.Documents (scoped storage API). No Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() usage exists. These are legacy declarations irrelevant on targetSdk=35. (Confidence: High)
findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32), WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=28), and uses requestLegacyExternalStorage=true, but all file operations use Capacitor Filesystem plugin with Directory.Documents (scoped storage on API 30+). No raw file path access found. The permissions are legacy artifacts from pre-scoped-storage era.
findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE from AndroidManifest.xml. Remove android:requestLegacyStorage="true" (only applies to API 29, irrelevant on targetSdk=35). The Capacitor Filesystem plugin already uses scoped storage via the SAF on API 30+ and works correctly without these permissions.

findings.evidence:
Manifest: READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 with maxSdkVersion=32. WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 with maxSdkVersion=28. requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11. Photo usage: SettingsModal.tsx:64 (logo upload, accept="image/*"), SettingsModal.tsx:134 (stamp upload, accept="image/*"), FinanceManager.tsx:267 (receipt scan, accept="image/*" capture="environment"). All image operations use <input type='file' accept='image/*'>: SettingsModal.tsx:64 (logo upload), SettingsModal.tsx:134 (stamp upload), FinanceManager.tsx:267 (receipt scan with capture='environment'). findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) despite all image handling being user-initiated single-file selection via <input type="file" accept="image/*"> — logo upload, stamp upload, and receipt scanning. findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions from AndroidManifest.xml — the app's image selection flows use <input type="file"> which invokes the system file picker without requiring broad storage permissions on any modern Android version.
